title: Swabbing Scats for DNA Sampling - Field Protocol
author: Anna MacDonald
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9agh2bw

steps.title: Document Sample Site
steps.instruction: Before touching the scat, record all necessary field data.

substeps.instruction: Photograph the scat
Assign a sample number
Record GPS coordinates
Record any other required field data

steps.title: Prepare for Sampling
steps.instruction: Ensure contamination control by using clean gloves.

substeps.instruction: Wear clean gloves for every sample
Change gloves as often as needed to avoid contamination

steps.title: Prepare Sterile Swab
steps.instruction: Select and verify a sterile swab and label the container.

substeps.instruction: Select a clean, unused swab
Check that the paper seal is undamaged; discard if damaged
Record the sample number and all other details on the swab tube label clearly to prevent smudging or washing off

steps.title: Open Swab Case
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the swab from its case without contaminating it.

substeps.instruction: Twist the swab to break the seal
Remove the swab without touching any part that was inside the collection tube or allowing it to touch other surfaces

steps.title: Moisten Swab if Necessary
steps.instruction: Pre-moisten the swab only if the scat is dry (older scats).

substeps.instruction: If scat retains obvious moisture, skip to swabbing
If scat is dry, open a 2ml tube of 1 x PBS
Briefly dip the swab into the PBS solution to moisten the outside (do not saturate or soak for a long time)
Immediately close the PBS tube to avoid contamination
Ensure only clean swabs are dipped into the PBS; do not dip swabs that have touched hands, ground, or scat

steps.title: Collect DNA Sample
steps.instruction: Swab the scat comprehensively before moving or disturbing it.

substeps.instruction: Roll the tip of the swab across the surface of the scat several times
Sample from each scat pellet and from the ends and middle of the scat

steps.title: Dry and Store Swab
steps.instruction: Air dry the swab and secure it in its container.

substeps.instruction: Briefly allow the swab to air dry without touching contaminating surfaces
Place the swab back into its container and ensure it is properly closed
Store containers in a box or bag, keeping them dry and out of direct sunlight
Store used swabs separately from unused swabs

steps.title: Post-Field Processing
steps.instruction: Process or store the samples to inhibit micro-organism growth.

substeps.instruction: Extract DNA from swabs in the lab as soon as possible
Alternatively, store swabs in dry conditions below 4°C (freeze if possible)
